mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in FEDFUNDS above 1% for three consecutive months predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return in the positive direction due to reduced policy rate uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: early stage of rate hike normalization
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the policy signal, or FEDFUNDS does not sustain the increase for the required period.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL exceeds 215, the expectation of future inflation increases discount rates on equity valuations, causing a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or near-zero when inflation exceeds 215, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS of at least 5% coinciding with a decline in UNRATE suggests strengthening labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings expectations and drive positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >=5% while UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for the labor signal (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month consecutive decline in GDPC1 above 12,000 billion chained dollars indicates weakening business demand, which predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for 2 consecutive months above 12,000
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the signal does not precede returns with sufficient lead time (lag > 0 days).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO above 97.5 triggers a regime of excess supply, lowering equity risk premia and producing a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or the effect is not significant (t-statistic < 1.96).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in HOUST (> 520) and PAYEMS (> 130,000) for three consecutive months indicate robust demand for goods and services, forecasting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% and PAYEMS increases by >4% over 3 months
failure_condition: Forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for both labor indicators (multivariate F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for four consecutive months in a regime of low inflation, it suggests accommodative policy, associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for 4 consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 215
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or the policy signal is not predictive (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in RSAFS of over 200 million dollars for two months indicates softening financial demand, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return in a contractionary regime.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >200 million for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after the signal (p-value > 0.05).
